## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. What happens next depends in part on the extensions an application imports.

If an extension does not explicitly declare support for free threading, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The declaration mechanism differs depending on whether the extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

For extension authors, declaring support and making code thread-safe are separate responsibilities. The declaration signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode; it does not, by itself, make the extension’s code thread-safe.
